title: Guardrails and Safe Deployment
summary: Guardrails are checks around a model: on what goes in, what comes out and what it is allowed to do. This lesson treats them as classifiers with thresholds, precision and recall, base rates and costs, then covers PII redaction and the design decisions (fail open or closed, human review) that make a deployment safe.
objectives: Describe input, output and action guardrails and combine layered checks with the right independence assumptions
Compute precision, recall, F1 and expected cost at several classifier thresholds
Use Bayes' rule to explain why a very accurate detector can still be wrong most of the time it fires
Estimate residual PII leakage after redaction and size a human review queue
Choose between fail-open and fail-closed behaviour for a given feature
prerequisites: You should know what a classifier threshold is and have met precision and recall ([Scoring Against References](/learn/evaluation/reference-scoring)), and understand prompt injection at a high level ([Prompt Injection and Trust Boundaries](/learn/prompt-and-context/prompt-injection)). Probability of independent events is used throughout.
